meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.en: to call for, to summon (a taxi, driver, police, doctor)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'звать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call, to summon', paired with 'вызывать'.

examples.text: Ты же не помнишь ничего. Ты вызвал трезвого водителя!
examples.trans: You don't remember anything, after all. You called a sober driver!

вызывать.gloss: to cause, to raise; to call

meanings.en: to cause, to arouse, to raise
meanings.note: вызывать подозрения = to raise suspicion
вызывать полицию / врача = to call the police / a doctor

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, упаковка маскирующая. Не вызывает подозрений.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, the packaging is camouflage. It doesn't raise suspicion.

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'maid' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть горничная.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always maid.
The chef immediately noticed where the maid was.

meanings.note: В гости = for a visit. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
+ instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'otherwise' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Пятьдесят метров, не больше. Иначе будет сигнал.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('personal, private').
Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('personal, private').

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Мне некогда = I have no time. Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'когда').

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Core Russian num meaning 'both' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You both leave here right now.
Get over here right now, quickly, both of you!

examples.text: Вы сейчас отсюда оба уходите. И больше сюда не возвращаетесь. Ясно?
examples.trans: You both leave here right now. And you never come back here again. Clear?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'from; of' in everyday speech.
Тошнит от = sick of. Core Russian prep meaning 'from; of' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'of the hotel' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это гематома, она и стала причиной потери памяти.
examples.trans: That is a hematoma, it became the cause of memory loss.

examples.text: Андрей, положи её к себе, а то и эту потеряю.
examples.trans: Andrey, put it in your pocket, or I will lose this one too.

examples.text: Я хотел бы просмотреть все документы по закупке продуктов.
examples.trans: I would like to review all the documents on food purchases.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Поговорить с + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: to show, to display, to broadcast
meanings.note: показывать по телевизору = to show on TV

examples.text: Ой, смотрите, Самсона по телевизору показывают! Уже несколько миллионов просмотров!
examples.trans: Oh, look, they're showing Samson on television! Several million views already!

meanings.note: Used in the singular. Borrowed in the Petrine era from German 'Polizei' / French 'police' (from Greek 'politeia', civil administration).

examples.text: Тут кнопки вызова: скорая, полиция и мы.
examples.trans: Here are the call buttons: ambulance, police, and us.

meanings.en: to weep, cry for a bit
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'плакать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to cry, weep a little', paired with 'плакать'.

examples.trans: She will cry a little and return.

meanings.note: the noun after it is genitive plural: пятьдесят метров

examples.trans: Fifty metres, no more. Otherwise there'll be a signal.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'joyfully'.

examples.text: Шеф, вы сейчас так радостно улыбаетесь!
examples.trans: Chef, you are smiling so joyfully now!

examples.text: Шеф, почему вы так радостно улыбаетесь?
examples.trans: Chef, why are you smiling so joyfully?

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'we will deliver around'.

examples.text: Разнесём их по номерам нашего отеля.
examples.trans: We will deliver them to the rooms of our hotel.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и разнести вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and we will deliver around on time.

related.gloss: to we will deliver around (prefixed perfective)
not to we will deliver around (negated infinitive)

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Marriage celebration. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'вадьба'). Common feminine noun meaning 'wedding' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Watch the movie Wedding on Skype.

examples.text: Макс, зачем ты соврал про нашу будущую свадьбу?
examples.trans: Max, why did you lie about our future wedding?
Then a wedding, and then kids!

meanings.note: The г sounds like в. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: + genitive plural: семь тысяч. Core Russian num meaning 'seven' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Там депозит на семь тысяч рублей!
examples.trans: There's a deposit for seven thousand roubles!

examples.text: Семь тысяч, давай сходим! Ты же любишь морепродукты.
examples.trans: Seven thousand, let's go! After all, you love seafood.

meanings.note: Informal. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'идеть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sit, to be sitting', paired with 'посидеть'.

examples.trans: Why are you sitting in the corner?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'коро'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: Совсем не. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').
Совсем не. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').

examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'традать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to suffer', paired with 'пострадать'.

examples.trans: People are suffering because of him.

examples.text: Ну и что? Он должен страдать, а нам нужна информация.
examples.trans: So what? He is supposed to suffer, and we need the information.

meanings.note: Direction. Core Russian adv meaning 'here (to this place)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: смотреть по телевизору = to watch on TV

examples.trans: And the television, by the way, is ours!

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, здесь же ребёнок, мы завтракаем. А телевизор, между прочим, наш!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, there's a child here, we're having breakfast. And the television, by the way, is ours!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

Просить у кого. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Уволен = fired (short participle). Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fire, to dismiss', paired with 'увольнять'.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Кому = at someone (dative). Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'лыбаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to smile', paired with 'улыбнуться'.

examples.trans: Nothing! He just sits there smiling.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'спокоиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to calm down', paired with 'успокаиваться'.

examples.text: Так, успокойтесь все. Сейчас за мной приедут.
examples.trans: Right, everyone calm down. They're coming for me any minute.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.
